blocks.text: Dear Mr. Villegas:

This letter sets down the terms on which our firm will act for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}} in the market entry assessment we discussed last week, and, once you have signed and returned the copy enclosed for that purpose, it will stand as the agreement between us. I have written it in plain language and at some length, because you are entitled to know exactly what you are agreeing to and not to sign something whose reach you have to guess at; and I would ask that, before you countersign, you read it against the conversation we had and tell me if anything set out here departs from what you understood us to have agreed.
The Assignment and Its Boundaries

What we have undertaken to do for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}} is to assess the case for the market entry you are weighing, and to do so in a way that gives your board a decision it can stand behind rather than a document it can merely file. We will describe the market as it is, size the opportunity it presents with the candor a real decision requires, weigh the ways into it together with the cost and the risk that each way carries, and set out a recommendation alongside the reasoning that leads to it, so that if you come to disagree with the recommendation you can see precisely where your judgment parts from ours.

The engagement covers our analysis and our counsel; it does not extend to carrying out whatever you decide, nor does it include legal, tax, regulatory, or accounting advice, on which you should continue to rely on the advisers who ordinarily provide it to you. Where our work touches those questions, what we offer is an informed view and not a professional opinion in their place, and we will say so plainly at the points where the distinction matters.

Our manner of working is deliberate. We begin by learning how your business runs and what the entry is meant to achieve for it, before we commit any finding to paper; we test what we are told against evidence we can gather for ourselves; and we bring you our thinking as it develops instead of holding it back for a single unveiling, so that the conclusions, when they come, contain no surprises. Where the evidence will not support a firm answer we will tell you so, and tell you what it would take to get one, because an assessment that overstates its own certainty is of no use to a board that has to act on it.
The People Who Will Do the Work

Jason Torres, a Principal of the firm, will lead the engagement and will be your point of contact for any matter of substance; he is direct by temperament and will tell you what the analysis shows whether or not it is what you were hoping to hear, which is the quality you are engaging him for. James Green will build and maintain the models and the exhibits on which the assessment rests, and will see to it that every figure we place in front of you can be traced back to where it came from. Deborah Gordon will lead the benchmarking and the market data that ground the recommendation, and she is at her most exacting where the numbers are concerned. I will keep my own hand on the work at the points where a judgment must be made about how far a conclusion can be pressed before it outruns the evidence, and nothing will leave the firm under our name without my having read it first.
Our Fee and the Basis of Our Charges

Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is {{fact:f:E-2012-001.fee}}, fixed for the scope set out above and covering the time of the people named. We will render invoices against that sum as the work proceeds, and each invoice will be payable within thirty days of your receipt of it. The fee does not include incidental costs such as travel or the reproduction of materials, which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they cost us; and should you ask us to widen the work materially beyond what this letter contemplates, I will raise the question of the fee with you and we will settle it together before that further work begins, so that nothing reaches you on an invoice you have not agreed to in advance.
Duration and Ending the Engagement

The engagement begins on {{fact:f:E-2012-001.start}} and is expected to run for about three months, though we will treat it as finished when the work is genuinely done and not merely when the calendar says that it should be. Either of us may bring it to an end on fourteen days' written notice to the other, for any reason or for none; if you are the one to do so, you will owe us for the work properly performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}} in the course of this work we will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of the engagement, an obligation that binds each member of the team, that survives the end of our involvement, and that covers the fact of the engagement as fully as it covers its substance. We ask the same of you in respect of the methods and the written materials we share with you, which are the firm's own and are given to you for your use and not for wider circulation.
The Limit of Our Responsibility

We will carry out the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the decision you will ultimately take or the conditions of the market you may enter, and so, except to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state. Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder of it will continue in force, unaffected by that provision's failure.

If this letter reflects the understanding we reached, please sign the enclosed copy where indicated below and return it to me, keeping the other for your own file; once your signed copy is in hand, Jason Torres will write to you within the week to arrange the first meetings and the initial requests for information, so that we can begin without losing time.
We are engaged to assess the market entry for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}}. The client wants a board-ready recommendation, not a survey. This memo sets who owns what, so we start in step.

The engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2012-001.start}}. Our sponsor on the client side is Mark Villegas, the Chief Financial Officer. Jason Torres holds the relationship; any client question of substance goes to him.

The first weeks have one job. We build a shared fact base before we form any view on entry. We do not write conclusions yet. Conclusions come later, and only once the client has agreed the facts they rest on.

The fact base has three parts. The size and shape of the market. The demand behind it. The economics of each way in. We hold each part to a source before we rely on it, and we keep what we know apart from what we assume.

One caution at the start. We are assessing the entry, not deciding it. The decision stays with the client's board. We keep our analysis and our recommendation clearly apart, so the board can weigh the evidence without being handed the answer.

The end product is a written assessment and a recommendation, with the workpapers behind them. That is the target we work back from. Everything in the plan below feeds one of those two things, and anything that does not, we drop.
How the work divides

items: Market and demand. Deborah Gordon owns the market sizing and the demand read. She builds the benchmark set first, since most of the analysis leans on it.
Entry economics. I own the economics of each way in and the models behind them. Every figure ties back to a source in the file.
Client interface. Jason Torres owns the relationship with Mark Villegas and how we present the work. He sets the cadence of the check-ins.
Data requests. We route every request to the client through one list, not several. I hold the list and keep it current.
Engagement file. We keep a shared file from this week. Sources go in as they arrive, so any number we later use can be traced.

blocks.text: This week

The priority this week is access. I send the client the first data request today. Deborah Gordon starts the market scan in parallel, so we are not idle while the data comes in. Jason Torres confirms the cadence of the check-ins with Mark Villegas and circulates the schedule to us.

We run a standing weekly check-in from next week, internal first and then with the client. It is short. Status, blockers, what we need from them. That keeps the requests to the client on one channel and the answers on the record.

I need two things from each of you before we meet again. First, the list of documents your area will need from the client. Second, the contacts you want to interview. Send both to me by Friday, so I can fold them into one request and not several.

I will keep the shared file current and post a short index of what has arrived and what is still outstanding, so no one has to ask me twice for the same status, and so Jason Torres has an accurate picture before each check-in with Mark Villegas.
Hi Mark,

The market entry assessment for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}} is on track, and we are about a quarter of the way through. The market data is in hand and the benchmark set is largely built. Deborah Gordon has finished the first pass on the demand read, and the early signal looks consistent with what we heard at kickoff. The next step is a working session to take you through the findings so far.

One item is outstanding on your side. We still need the regional sales breakdown your finance team agreed to send. Deborah Gordon needs it to close the segment comparison, and without it we would be presenting around a gap. If you can have it to me by the middle of next week, we can hold the session as planned and keep the review on its timeline.

For the session, our attendees will be Jason Torres, Deborah Gordon, and James Green, with you, Mark Villegas, and whoever on your side owns the sales figures. Jason Torres will lead it and take you through the read. Let me know a day next week that suits you, and I will hold it and send an agenda round once the date is fixed.
Best
Working Session Minutes: Market Entry Assessment for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}}

These minutes record the working session our team held with the client to review where the market entry assessment for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}} now stands and to agree what we take up next; they are meant as the shared record we all work from, and if any of us reads them differently, please say so within the week so that we can correct them together.
Present

items: James Green, Senior Associate, Calderwood Partners

blocks.text: What we discussed

We opened by walking Mark Villegas through the market picture as it now stands, and James Green took the group through the demand read and the benchmark set that underpins it, noting where the data is firm and where we are still filling gaps, so that no one left the room more confident than the evidence allows. We agreed that the shape of the opportunity is clearer than it was at the outset, that the near-term demand looks real, and that the questions worth our attention from here are narrower and sharper than the ones we began with.

I then took the group through the benchmarking, which is the part of the work I own, and we looked together at how the comparable entries elsewhere have fared, so that we could anchor our own estimates against something other than our own optimism; we agreed that the peer evidence supports the case for the entry in broad terms while cautioning us on the pace at which the demand is likely to build, and that our sizing should reflect that slower build rather than assume the market arrives all at once.

Much of the remaining time went to the regional sales breakdown we are still waiting on from the client's finance team, since it is the piece that lets us close the segment comparison, and Mark Villegas undertook to have it to us by the middle of next week; we were candid with one another that until it arrives our sizing carries a wider band than we would like, and Jason Torres was clear that we would show that band honestly and not paper over it. We also talked through the ways into the market, and while we did not settle on one, we did agree on the handful of criteria against which we will weigh them once the analysis is complete.

Before we closed, we set out what each of us carries forward from here, and we agreed that nothing would be put in front of the client's board as settled until the underlying figures had been through both our review and theirs.
What we each take forward

rows: Send the regional sales breakdown to the team
Close the segment comparison once the sales data is in
Firm up the entry economics and tie each figure to a source
Confirm with the client the criteria for weighing the entry options

blocks.text: We will reconvene once the sales data is in and the segment comparison is closed, and I will circulate these minutes to everyone today; unless a correction reaches me within the week, they will stand as our record of what we agreed.
Status Report: Market Entry Assessment for {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}}

Prepared for the leadership of {{fact:f:E-2012-001.client}} by the Calderwood engagement team. This report covers the period since our last update and looks ahead to the work that follows. The team on your engagement is Jason Torres, who leads it, James Green, and Deborah Gordon.
Where we stand

The engagement is at its midpoint and on plan. The market work is substantially done. The entry economics are in draft. One data dependency on your side is holding up the segment detail, and it is the main thing to watch.

The recommendation is not yet formed, and at this stage it should not be. We are still assembling the fact base your board will need to decide. What follows is progress against the plan, not conclusions.
Four things in a line. The market is understood, the economics are drafted, the one gap is your sales data, and the fee is tracking to plan. The detail follows.
What we completed this period

The market work is the bulk of this period. It is now substantially done and documented. We would rather hand your board a narrow, sourced picture than a broad one we cannot stand behind, and the work reflects that.

items: Deborah Gordon completed the market sizing and the demand read. Both are documented, and each input is sourced in the engagement file.
The benchmark set is built and reconciled against outside data, so the comparisons rest on figures we can defend.
The entry economics are in draft. Each way into the market is modeled, and every figure ties back to a source in the file.
We held a working session with your team. We agreed the criteria against which the entry options will be weighed once the sizing is closed.

blocks.text: One point on method, since it shapes what you can rely on. Every figure in the draft carries a source in the engagement file. Where a number is our estimate rather than a fact, it is labeled as an estimate, with the band around it. Your team can trace any line back to where it came from, and we would encourage the finance owners to do exactly that before the board sees it.
What comes next

The next period turns on the regional sales breakdown from your finance team. Once it is in, Deborah Gordon closes the segment comparison and we finalize the sizing. I then firm the economics against the completed sizing, so the numbers move together and not in pieces.

With the sizing closed, Jason Torres will bring you a first view of the entry options and the criteria we will weigh them against. That view comes ahead of the recommendation itself, so you can steer the analysis before it hardens.

We would ask two things of your team in the same window. Confirm the finance owner for the sales data, so Deborah Gordon has one contact and not several. Flag any constraint on the entry that we should treat as fixed, so we do not model options your board has already ruled out.
Budget

The engagement is a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2012-001.fee}}. At the midpoint the work is tracking within it, and we see nothing in what remains that would change that, provided the scope holds. Should you ask us to widen the work, we would raise the fee with you before taking it on, as the engagement letter sets out.
Risks and what we are watching

items: The outstanding sales data is the one real dependency. Until it arrives, the segment sizing carries a wider band than we want. If it slips past next week, the final read slips with it, and we will tell you rather than quietly absorb the delay.
The entry options are still open. We will not narrow them until the sizing is closed, so the board should expect a set of choices, not a single answer, at the next review.

The peer evidence points to a slower demand build than the early market read suggested. That is a finding, not a problem, but it will shape the economics, and we are flagging it early so it does not land as a surprise in the recommendation.
Nothing else on the engagement is off plan at this point.

blocks.text: We will send the next update after the working session that follows the segment close. If anything here needs discussion before then, Jason Torres is your point of contact.
